title: Basic vowels
intro: Korean vowels are built from one long line plus short marks. A vowel is never written alone: when a syllable starts with a vowel sound, the silent letter ㅇ fills the first position (아, 오).

title: Basic consonants
intro: Ten plain consonants. ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ and ㅈ are soft: they sit between English g/k, d/t, b/p and j/ch, with almost no puff of air. Each one is spoken here with the vowel ㅏ (가, 나, 다).

title: Aspirated consonants
intro: Four consonants with a strong puff of air. Hold your palm in front of your mouth: you should feel air on ㅋ, ㅌ, ㅍ and ㅊ, and almost none on ㄱ, ㄷ, ㅂ and ㅈ.

title: Double (tense) consonants
intro: Five tense consonants, written as doubled letters. Tighten your throat and release the sound sharply, with no air. Russian к, т and п have no puff of air, so they are a good starting point for ㄲ, ㄸ and ㅃ.

title: Compound vowels
intro: Eleven vowels made by combining basic ones. Several sound the same in everyday speech: ㅐ and ㅔ, and the trio ㅙ, ㅚ and ㅞ. Learn to read them all; the spelling comes with vocabulary.
